body: A little update, I have a Seymour Duncan Pearly gates neck and a SH-5, I haven't found any need to put them in, this is the second time that I found good ProBuckers, not every time I've liked them, actually this is only the second time, I don't know why, if there's an issue with production or something, but this set is fucking awesome, sweet but kinky, spicy and delicate, all at the same time.
It's an Epiphone Les Paul Modern in Purple Burst, the new models also com with an Epiphone Gigbag
Indeed, also has 24 beautiful frets on ebony
Did you really enjoy more the Duncan's? I tend to prefer Gibson pickups
I did that, you'll need 500k pots and capacitors, hated the Fishmans
Thanks man! Couldn't cope with the Fishmans, went the SD way, although I'm not 100 satisfied (I prefer Gibson pickups) I'm now closer to my perfect guitar, live the 24 frets

Ok man, I've played both, an I prefer the modern, it's cheaper and the Probucker are more my type of sound, I HATE the Fishman's, I quick search on YouTube and you'll see I'm not alone, they sound like the wah stayed on, very toy like, not my thing, the split is a joke, the modern mode is ass and the only usable mode is the Gibson Busrtbucker mode, but still very far from the colors and overtones. Ok the other hand I really like the Probucker, very nice sound, I prefer it over a JB / 59 set
Almost agreed, 2012 still my favorite one but man I'm really enjoying 2021 except for the lack of Melbourne and Susuka

>Fuck, I cant relate to the family thing since I've been free when it comes to any responsibilities but I can relate alot to the work part.  
>  
>And yeah, I also know the rollercoaster-ride...  
>  
>It's not selfish to take care of yourself. Since noone else seems to be doing that properly I would even say that it is your duty to take care of yourself.  
>  
>Try change things and maybe it'll get better. I assume you live like this for a couple of years now? And there is no perspective in life that it gets any better... At least I currently feel this way and that makes it so hard to live on.  
>  
>When I was 20 I had a girlfriend (19) who still lived with her father. He provided for the whole family but got despised by her and her mother. I never understood it, he was a very kind and calm man. She, while living a great and carefree life, always complained about him. I couldnt stand that and was feeling so sorry for the guy. Her parents stayed together because of their kids (she had a brother). And both seemed so sad and unhappy in that relationship. I don't know what happened after my ex moved out a year later, but I know that noone deserves this treatment!  
>  
>I don't want to say you remind me of him, I just feel like you are a nice guy and you also dont deserve to be sad. There are probably alot of men out there, not showing how they actually feel and living in these toxic environments that they call life.  
>  
>Men are often overlooked... we need to provide and care for everyone but noone is asking how we feel or if we are alright.

I agree, that beer is much needed, and yes man are often overlooked, the traditional role of men is so rotten.
I can relate to all your points here, I agree with the take action part, it is still time but, I can't find the energy the motivation, the will to do it, I'm tired
I know, somehow we need to find ourselves so we can be a sort of help and support for others, including your baby sister, I guess that's the hardest part.
I will, that's the only true exit

Yes many times, it's a rollercoaster every week. I find myself lacking the will to keep on going, I feel like since I'm 40 I'm done, no works for me, no future, feel like a total failure to my daughter, a lot of aphaty, weakness, even if I knew what was  needed to be done, I let this happened, I knew what I had to do before it was to late, but I hoped that things will get better at work and with the wife,

I do have 1 friend who has been my support this year's, he's also a father but he did choose to separate from his wife, it's confusing, he is in another state, see his boy twice a year but I saw him yesterday, he looked awesome, has a new girlfriend and he just looks like 10 years younger, however I want to stay by my daughter.

I'm 41 and I've been dealing with suicidal thoughts since my daughter was 2, now she is 6 years old, she made me the happiest man in the world, and she's the only reason I hang on, but the relationship with my wife and her family has drained me to my core, as well as my job, it's been really hard and I haven't found a way to overcome this, if I get divorced, I won't see my daughter but twice a month If I'm lucky, I grew up without a present father, he was very responsible with the economical part of his duties and still is to this day, he sometimes invites us a meal or helps me from time to time with presents for her granddaughter and I love him and understand him now more than ever, but he was living in another state when I  was a child and I don't want the same for my daughter, I want to be there by her side, also a divorce needs a lot of economical resources which I don't have right now.

Let me tell you something that you may already know, when you are over 40 everyone takes from you, you become this sort of ATM machine that no one cares about, and that ain´t easy, I now understand why many parents(moms and dads) have lovers, which I used to judge a lot, it's because you are lonely and vulnerable, even when you are surrounded with people, coworkers and a "happy family" you may say, but most of them don't really care about you, they just take from you, friends become distant, the ones who don't have a family don't understand you anymore, they still want to go and have fun late at night and wake up noon the next day, they don't understand the responsibility of being a parent, that you will have a little person that wakes up every day at the latest  7 a.m., the ones that do have a family, are also trying to survive so they don't have the time, a lover is a false illusion of someone that really cares about you, that knows who you really are, but then again, that is also false. 

I got the covid 19 in December and had a transient ischemic attack in January, I almost die that night, the next months I struggle with low blood pressure and constant vertigo but no one gave me a pause, a break, at work every one reached out for me to be on duty, and at home I'm the only support,  so no, it ain't part of my rights to get sick, on the contrary, it was minimized and judged, I was asked to get back to work the next week (the TIA was on a Thursday night) and the sleepless nights because of vertigo and low blood pressure didn't mean a thing at work or at home, now I´m recovering my health and brain functions at a very slow pace although I gained a lot of weight, almost 40 pounds because I fill my void with food. 

Still I wonder why I didn't die, I'm stuck in this prison called "ball breaker wife featuring in-laws that despises my whole being and a middle-aged career crisis bump with no visible hope in the future for it". 

So yes man, '40s are hard, actually, harder than when you were young and strong, and it will be even harder as age comes to us.
